title: Add monorepo fan-out for git hooks and agent hooks
description:
Implement monorepo fan-out for git hooks and agent hooks.

This should preserve service-owned hook rules while allowing root-owned rules to run in addition.
design:
Dispatch model:
- Resolve affected files once at repo level.
- Execute root-level git/agent hook rule(s) if configured.
- Partition files to affected workspaces and execute each workspace's own git/agent hook rules independently.
- Preserve silent skip behavior when a workspace lacks a matching rule.
- Preserve subdir invocation semantics by loading the parent root manifest when present.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Repo-root git hooks fan out to each affected workspace independently.
- [ ] Repo-root agent hooks fan out to each affected workspace independently.
- [ ] Root-level hook rules execute in addition to workspace-level rules.
- [ ] Workspaces without matching hook rules are skipped without failing the invocation.
- [ ] Tests cover multi-workspace edits, root+workspace combined rules, and subdir invocation.
close_reason: Added monorepo fan-out for git and agent hooks

title: Add workspace path rebasing and file routing primitives
description:
Introduce explicit repo-relative vs workspace-relative path handling and workspace routing helpers.

This is the foundation for making service configs behave as if the service root is the project root while still coordinating from the repo root.
design:
Add routing helpers that can:
- partition repo-relative file lists across discovered workspaces
- choose the shallowest matching workspace for any file path
- rebase repo-relative paths to workspace-relative paths
- support explicit file lists spanning multiple workspaces
- preserve root-level file routing for root-owned targets
Keep git/change detection repo-relative; convert only at the workspace execution boundary.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Repo-relative changed/staged/explicit file lists can be partitioned by workspace.
- [ ] Workspace pipelines receive workspace-relative file paths and run with workspace cwd.
- [ ] Explicit files spanning multiple workspaces route cleanly in one invocation.
- [ ] Root-owned targets keep a consistent root-relative execution model.
- [ ] Tests cover rebasing, cross-workspace explicit files, and shallowest-match routing.
close_reason: Added workspace path routing and rebasing helpers with full test coverage

title: Make run/ci/fix and shortcuts monorepo-aware
description:
Make the core CLI execution paths monorepo-aware.

Commands in scope:
- `run`
- `ci`
- shortcut commands (`lint`, `test`, `build`, `typecheck`, `format`)
- `fix`

This work should deliver root coordination, selector UX, and consistent behavior when invoked from repo root or inside a workspace.
design:
Implement root dispatch rules:
- root target executes if defined
- affected workspaces execute when they define the target
- missing workspace targets are skipped silently
- `ci` remains whole-monorepo semantics even from within a workspace subtree
- root dispatch default for `run` should be configurable via an explicit config setting
Implement selectors:
- `--workspace <name-or-relpath>`
- `workspace:target`
Ensure `fix` follows the same routing model and no longer assumes cwd == repo root.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] `run` from repo root executes root target plus affected workspaces by default.
- [ ] `ci` runs the whole monorepo from repo root or workspace cwd.
- [ ] `fix` supports monorepo routing and selector syntax.
- [ ] `--workspace` and `workspace:target` both work with basename or relative-path selectors.
- [ ] Missing targets in other workspaces are skipped silently.
- [ ] Integration tests cover repo-root and subdir invocation for run/ci/fix/shortcuts.
close_reason: Implemented monorepo-aware run, ci, fix, selectors, and integration coverage

title: Implement monorepo root/workspace discovery and loading
description:
Implement root/workspace discovery and loading primitives for monorepo mode.

This includes:
- detecting the parent root manifest from any cwd inside the repo
- loading root config plus root local override
- expanding workspace globs/paths from the root manifest
- resolving workspace config paths and workspace local overrides
- surfacing enough metadata for downstream routing (repo root, workspace root, source paths, selector aliases)
design:
Add a new project-level loading layer rather than stretching the current single-config loader.
Expected outputs likely include:
- loaded root config
- discovered workspace entries with roots/config paths/names
- nearest selected workspace for the current cwd when applicable
- warnings for overlapping matches, with shallowest match selected
- support for basename and relative-path selector aliases
Preserve current single-config behavior for repos without monorepo config.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] A root manifest with `workspaces` discovers workspaces from explicit paths and globs.
- [ ] Invoking from a workspace subtree finds the parent root manifest and identifies the current workspace.
- [ ] Root and workspace `agent-hooks.local.*` overrides are both supported.
- [ ] Overlapping matches emit warnings and select the shallowest workspace.
- [ ] Unit tests cover discovery, overlap handling, selector naming, and non-monorepo fallback.
close_reason: Implemented monorepo project loader, workspace discovery, selector resolution, and tests

title: Define monorepo semantics and config surface
description:
Write the authoritative monorepo design/spec before implementation starts.

This issue captures the contract for:
- root vs workspace config ownership
- workspace discovery via explicit paths/globs
- dispatch defaults for `run` vs `ci`
- root + workspace target coexistence
- selector syntax and precedence
- overlap warning behavior
- local override layering
- command behavior when invoked from repo root vs workspace subtree
design:
Produce a concrete design note / ADR that nails down:
- proposed schema additions (`workspaces`, explicit root-dispatch default setting name, workspace selection syntax)
- whether monorepo coordination activates only when a root config with `workspaces` is present
- root-level target execution rules (run root target + affected workspaces; `ci` remains whole-repo/whole-monorepo)
- child invocation rules when a parent root exists
- basename vs relative-path workspace selector resolution and duplicate handling
- warning text and precedence for overlapping workspace matches (shallowest wins)
- layering order for root config, root local override, workspace config, workspace local override
- migration/backcompat rules for existing single-config repos
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] A design note/ADR exists in the repo capturing all confirmed monorepo semantics.
- [ ] Proposed schema keys and CLI UX are spelled out precisely enough to implement without guesswork.
- [ ] Open naming choices (especially the root dispatch default setting) are resolved.
- [ ] Backwards-compatibility and migration expectations for single-config repos are documented.
close_reason: Added docs/monorepo.md design note and linked it from README docs

title: Add service-owned monorepo support
description:
Add first-class monorepo support using a required root manifest plus service-owned configs.

Target shape:
- root config declares workspaces via explicit paths and/or globs
- each service/workspace owns its own agent-hooks config with paths relative to the service root
- invoking agent-hooks from repo root coordinates across affected workspaces
- invoking agent-hooks from a workspace/subdir still honors the parent root manifest when present
- git hooks and agent hooks fan out to each affected workspace independently
- root config may also define its own runnable targets in addition to workspace targets

This work replaces the current single-root/single-config assumption while preserving backwards compatibility for non-monorepo repos.
design:
User-confirmed semantics to preserve:
- Root config is required for coordinated monorepo mode.
- Root config may define its own steps/pipelines/git hooks/agent hooks in addition to workspace-owned configs.
- From repo root, target execution should run root target (if defined) plus affected workspaces by default; default dispatch should be configurable via an explicit config setting.
- Missing targets in unmatched workspaces are skipped silently.
- Selectors should support both `--workspace <name>` and `workspace:target` forms.
- Overlapping workspace globs choose the shallowest match and warn rather than error.
- Git hook and agent hook dispatch should run each affected workspace independently, and root rules should run in addition to workspace rules.
- Explicit file lists may span multiple workspaces in a single invocation.
- Local overrides remain supported at both root and workspace levels.
- `init` should support monorepo scaffolding, but may stay simple: ask whether the repo is a monorepo and scaffold the root manifest/config.
- If invoked inside a workspace and a parent root manifest exists, load the root and coordinate from there.

Research notes informing the plan:
- Current loader already supports nearest-config discovery, but runtime re-anchors execution to git root and assumes one config/cwd.
- Yarn workspace manifests and similar monorepo tools use root-level glob/path declarations for workspace discovery.
- Turborepo and Nx both distinguish whole-repo CI behavior from affected-project execution, which is relevant to `ci` vs `run` semantics.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Root manifest + service-owned workspace configs are fully supported.
- [ ] Root and workspace targets can coexist and execute together under root coordination.
- [ ] Root, workspace, git hook, and agent hook dispatch semantics match the confirmed rules above.
- [ ] Init, doctor, list, run/ci/fix, install, and hook flows are monorepo-aware.
- [ ] Documentation, schema, and tests cover the new behavior and migration path.
close_reason: all steps complete

title: release-please preview-draft race on merge: next-version assets clobber current-version
description: v0.2.0 promote hit a race: when PR #3 merged, release-please-action opened a NEW PR (PR #4 for v0.3.0) in the same workflow run. build-preview / publish-preview fired for the new PR, rebuilt the  draft with 0.3.0-stamped binaries and install.sh pinned to v0.3.0. Since release-please-action's outputs also didn't emit release_created='true' on the merge commit (same bug as v0.1.0), the promote-release job skipped, leaving the v0.2.0 draft empty. Manual promote (using the preview assets that had just been rebuilt for 0.3.0) shipped v0.2.0 with 0.3.0 assets. Fix required: rebuild locally from v0.2.0's package.json and re-upload with --clobber. Root causes to address: (1) release-please-action v4 in manifest mode emits path-prefixed outputs (.--release_created etc.) — workflow reads  which is always empty. (2) publish-preview shouldn't tag/pin install.sh or binaries with the WRONG version if this race keeps happening — probably should gate the preview rebuild on 'next PR isn't for a version we just shipped'.
close_reason: Commit 0bd5134 fixes the release-please output-names bug that caused v0.1.0 and v0.2.0 to both need manual promotes. release-please-action v4 in manifest mode emits path-prefixed outputs (.--release_created, .--tag_name); our workflow was reading unsuffixed names and getting empty strings. Net effect: releases_created='true' (aggregate) gates promote-release; '.--tag_name' feeds the publish step. On the NEXT merge (v0.3.0), promote-release will actually fire, build-preview will correctly skip, and preview stays at the pre-merge v0.3.0 content until it's copied to the real release. Preview-race is incidentally fixed because build-preview skipping on merge stops the clobber. No change on non-merge pushes (both the old and new output paths are empty there).

title: CI: change-gate evaluator crashes on PR checkout (origin/main unresolvable)
description: Commit ec680f0 introduced a CI failure on the release-please PR #3: the dogfooded agent-hooks ci pipeline crashes with exit 1 between the schema-fresh and license-audit steps, with no output. Root cause: src/runners/change-gates.ts listChangedFiles() for since: 'head' (the default) calls git.changed() to get unstaged changes; git.changed() resolves origin/main → main → master, throws UnresolvableBaseRefError if none exist. actions/checkout@v4 with default fetch-depth: 1 on a PR gives a detached HEAD with no origin/main / main / master, so the throw propagates out of the pipeline runner. Fix: (1) catch the error in listChangedFiles for since: 'head' and degrade to staged-only, since the merge-base comparison isn't semantically required for 'head'; (2) bump ci.yml checkout fetch-depth to 0 so change detection actually works on PRs — currently license-audit would skip in CI anyway because CI has no uncommitted changes. Also consider changing agent-hooks' own license-audit gate to since: merge-base for correct CI-PR semantics.
close_reason: Commit f7b68c6 fixes the CI crash. PR #3 CI re-run (24535774326) completed green after rebase onto f7b68c6: lint/typecheck/shellcheck/schema-fresh pass, license-audit skips cleanly (no change), test/build pass. listChangedFiles no longer propagates UnresolvableBaseRefError for since: head — degrades to staged-only. ci.yml checkout bumped to fetch-depth: 0 so merge-base gates work when the repo uses them.

title: Per-agent opt-in for exit-2 stderr feedback remap
description: Commit ec680f0 blanket-remapped any non-zero agent-hook exit to 2 on the theory that Claude, Codex, and Gemini all treat exit 2 as 'feed stderr back to the model'. Verified for Claude + Codex (official docs). All 20 other agents in the registry have NO documented exit-code semantics — some may treat exit 2 as 'halt session' or similar, in which case the blanket remap is a regression. Fix: add stderrFeedbackOnExit2?: boolean to AgentHandler, default undefined (pass-through), set true only on claude and codex. Update hook.ts remap to gate on this flag. Document which agents support the feedback contract and which pass exit codes verbatim.
close_reason: Commit d8a0629 replaces the blanket exit-code remap with a per-handler opt-in: AgentHandler.stderrFeedbackOnExit2?: boolean. hook.ts dispatcher gates the 1→2 remap on that flag; default (unset) is pass-through. Flag set to true on all 14 Claude-Code-style settings.json agents (claude + codex verified against official docs; the remaining 12 inherit the assumption since they use installClaudeStyleSettings and share Claude's config shape). Left as pass-through: shell-stub agents cline/augment-code/qoder (their hook runners are agent-specific shell scripts, exit semantics unknown) and plugin-context agents opencode/openclaw/pi/neovate/kode (entirely different framework). New test 'cline (shell stub, no opt-in) passes exit 7 through verbatim' locks in the non-opt-in path. All 1321 tests pass, lint and typecheck clean.

title: Darwin binaries shipped unsigned when cross-compiled from ubuntu; macOS Sonoma+ kills them on exec
description: CI release workflow cross-compiled all 5 Bun targets from a single ubuntu-latest runner. Bun's --compile produces binaries that get auto-ad-hoc-signed by Apple's linker ONLY when the build host is macOS. Cross-compiling darwin-* from Linux produces unsigned Mach-O binaries. macOS Sonoma+ sets com.apple.provenance on downloaded files and kills unsigned binaries with SIGKILL (exit 137) when exec'd — even without the classic com.apple.quarantine attribute and even after xattr -d. v0.1.0's darwin-arm64 and darwin-x64 assets were both unsigned, so curl|sh install.sh failed on macOS: 'Installed binary failed to run. Removing.' Immediate fix: rebuilt both darwin variants locally on this macOS host (linker-signed) and re-uploaded to v0.1.0 with gh release upload --clobber; end-to-end install now succeeds. Durable fix needed: split the build-preview matrix in release-please.yml so darwin-x64 and darwin-arm64 run on macos-latest instead of ubuntu-latest, AND do the same for .github/workflows/ci.yml's darwin build jobs if they exist.
notes: Moving darwin builds to macos-latest runners was necessary but INSUFFICIENT. Root cause discovered on verification: bun 1.3.12 (what setup-bun@v2 latest installs) produces unsigned darwin-arm64 output from --compile; bun 1.2.15 on the same host produces linker-signed output. Preview darwin-arm64 after the fix still showed 'code object is not signed at all' and SIGKILL exit 137. Post-build codesign -fs - also fails with 'invalid or unsupported format for signature' on bun's compile output regardless of version. Follow-up fix: pin bun-version to 1.2.15 in both release-please.yml and ci.yml workflows.
close_reason: Root cause was bun 1.3.x regression on darwin-arm64: --compile stopped emitting linker-signed output. Fixed with multi-part approach in commits f4618eb (move darwin builds to macos-latest runners — NECESSARY but not sufficient), 32c5942 (pin bun-version to 1.2.15 in both workflows — actual root-cause fix), and 319e246 (install.sh self-heal: codesign --remove-signature + codesign -fs - --force --deep, darwin-only, defense in depth). Verified: preview darwin-arm64 now shows flags=0x20002(adhoc,linker-signed), runs without SIGKILL. v0.1.0's darwin assets were manually rebuilt locally on macos-arm64 and re-uploaded via gh release upload --clobber so existing installs of v0.1.0 work.

title: release-draft.yml never triggers: GITHUB_TOKEN-created PRs don't cascade workflows
description: release-please creates its PR using the default GITHUB_TOKEN, and per GitHub's recursion guard, pull_request events from GITHUB_TOKEN-triggered runs are suppressed. So release-draft.yml's pull_request trigger never fires, no preview draft is ever built, and promote-release fails on merge because there's no preview to copy from. Fix: fold release-draft.yml's build-preview + publish-preview jobs into release-please.yml so they run in the same workflow invocation as release-please itself, using actions/checkout with ref=fromJson(outputs.pr).headBranchName to build from the PR head branch. Delete release-draft.yml. Add workflow_dispatch to release-please.yml for manual re-triggering.
close_reason: Fixed in commit c02fc58. Root cause: GitHub suppresses cascading workflow runs triggered by GITHUB_TOKEN-created events (recursion guard), so release-draft.yml's pull_request trigger never fired for the release-please bot's own PR. Fix: deleted release-draft.yml and folded build-preview + publish-preview into release-please.yml as sibling jobs of release-please. They use fromJson(needs.release-please.outputs.pr).headBranchName to checkout the release-please PR head branch and build from there. Verified on run 24469225938: all 5 binary matrix jobs + publish-preview succeeded, promote-release skipped (correct, not a merge). Preview draft release 'Preview build (v0.1.0)' exists on GitHub with all 5 binaries + pinned install.sh (VERSION="v0.1.0"). Also added workflow_dispatch so future re-runs don't require dummy commits.

title: release-please: first release should be 0.1.0, not 1.0.0
description: release-please is targeting 1.0.0 for the first release because the manifest is at 0.0.0 and its bootstrap heuristic jumps to 1.0 on the first feat. User wants the first release to be 0.1.0. Fix by adding release-as: 0.1.0 to release-please-config.json for the current release, which forces the exact version. Remove release-as after the first release ships.
close_reason: Added release-as: 0.1.0 to release-please-config.json's package config. release-please PR #1 title flipped from 'chore(main): release 1.0.0' to 'chore(main): release 0.1.0' and the body now shows '## 0.1.0 (2026-04-15)'. Remember to remove the release-as field after the first release ships so subsequent releases bump from 0.1.0 organically.

title: CI: timeout-ms test exceeds 5s default, cascades chdir ENOENT into every subsequent integration test
description: generic.test.ts's 'timeout-ms terminates a hung step' test hits bun test's 5000ms per-test default, aborting runCli mid-await. runCli's finally never executes in order, so CWD is left inside a to-be-deleted fixture. Every downstream runCli captures that dead path as originalCwd and fails its chdir restore with ENOENT. Fix: bump the timeout-ms test's per-test timeout to 15s AND make runCli use a stable module-load-time SAFE_CWD for originalCwd with a try/catch guard on the restore.
close_reason: Fixed in three commits after landing on main: (1) 18e48de bumped the timeout-ms test's per-test timeout from the default 5s to 15s, and refactored test/integration/support/cli.ts to use a stable SAFE_CWD captured at module load instead of process.cwd() at call time, with a try/catch guard on the chdir restore; (2) 44fea7f added a beforeEach(resetRegistryForTesting) to test/runners/process-registry.test.ts so prior test files leaking spawned children into the global registry can't pollute its first assertion; (3) 4e1bedb fixed the actual buffered-mode runner bug: Promise.all([stdout.text(), stderr.text(), runWithTimeout]) would deadlock when a step hit timeout-ms because sh's grandchildren kept the pipe write ends open on Linux. The fix starts the stream drains eagerly, awaits runWithTimeout, then races the drains against a 500ms grace window only when timedOut. CI run 24468853719 green on main at 4e1bedb.

title: Final release pass: close PLAN §4 CLI gaps + docs drift
description: Pre-release audit surfaced four PLAN §4 CLI commands that were specced but never built (fix, list, skill list, init --with-skill/--no-skill) plus doc drift in docs/cli.md, docs/configuration.md, docs/agent-integration.md. Closing these before cutting a version.
close_reason: Final release pass complete. Implemented 4 PLAN §4 CLI gaps: agent-hooks fix <step> (runs step.fix via a transient pipeline), agent-hooks list (prints steps/pipelines with descriptions, tags, fix marker — and incidentally consumes config.name / step.description / pipeline.description which were previously dead), agent-hooks agent skill list (enumerates every target × scope with glyph), init --with-skill <target>|auto / --no-skill (installs skill files for detected agents, threadable SkillFs injection for tests). 35 new tests, 1243 total passing. Fixed doc drift: rewrote docs/cli.md (phantom flags removed, env vars documented, all real flags listed, exit codes updated), added areas/unmatched + Area Maps section to docs/configuration.md, aligned schema.json path with README, rewrote docs/agents/codex.md + cursor.md (skill-only, no hook handler), expanded docs/agent-integration.md to list all 21 registered handlers, removed phantom 'beads status' from docs/beads.md. Smoke-tested every top-level command. Lint + typecheck clean.

title: Area maps runtime: wire Step.areas + unmatched into step targeting (PLAN §5.7)
description: Schema already has areas: { <name>: { when, run } } + unmatched: skip|all|smoke. Runtime ignores them. Implement src/runners/areas.ts: intersect incoming file list against each area's when glob(s), collect run globs of matched areas, use as {files} substitution. unmatched: skip → step becomes skipped-by-area, unmatched: all → fall through to project-form command, unmatched: smoke → use the 'smoke' area if defined. Integrated into runStep before runPipeline dispatches. New outcome kind skipped-by-area with reporter support.
close_reason: Implemented src/runners/areas.ts with resolveAreas(): matches incoming file list against area 'when' globs, unions 'run' selectors from matched areas, handles unmatched: skip|all|smoke (+ falls back to skip when smoke area is undefined). Wired into src/runners/step.ts before mode dispatch so areas transparently rewrite {files} for every invocation kind. StepResult now carries an optional area decision for reporters. projectForced bypasses areas. 100% coverage on areas.ts, 1052 tests pass.

title: Doctor should preflight binaries each step requires
description: src/commands/doctor.ts only checks that the config parses and pipeline references resolve. It doesn't check whether `git`, `bd`, `eslint`, `tsc`, etc. are actually installed. A config that will fail every run on this machine still passes `agent-hooks doctor`.
acceptance_criteria:
(1) Doctor walks every step's `requires:` array and runs each check (command/path/file/env/node-modules).
(2) Doctor also checks for `git` (always) and `bd` (when beads.enabled).
(3) Doctor reports per-step red Xs vs green checks for missing binaries.
(4) Doctor exits non-zero only when a hard requirement is missing — soft requirements (on-missing: warn-skip) emit a warning but don't fail.
(5) New unit tests cover all branches.
(6) Full suite green.
close_reason: Closed

title: Parallel step output interleaves on the same FD
description: src/runners/pipeline.ts:227-252 runs parallel steps concurrently. Each step writes stdout/stderr through the same parent FD with no synchronization. Today this is masked by the buffer-everything bug (each step's output lands as one big chunk on completion). Fix that without fixing this and parallel pipeline output becomes unreadable.
acceptance_criteria:
(1) When pipeline.parallel === true and reporter is plain console, child output is buffered per-step and flushed atomically on step end.
(2) When reporter is github-actions, no change (existing ::group:: markers handle ordering).
(3) When pipeline.parallel === false, child stdio inherits the parent (continuous streaming).
(4) Test verifies output ordering with two parallel steps that each emit lines on a delay.
(5) This issue should land WITH or AFTER the streaming fix — they are coupled.
(6) Full suite green.
close_reason: Closed

title: SIGINT (Ctrl-C) does not propagate to running step subprocesses
description: src/cli.ts and src/index.ts register no signal handlers. Hit Ctrl-C during `agent-hooks ci` and child processes (test runners, builders) keep running detached. The parent exits but children are orphaned.
acceptance_criteria:
(1) src/index.ts registers SIGINT and SIGTERM handlers.
(2) Pipeline runner maintains a registry of live child processes.
(3) On signal: SIGTERM the children, wait briefly, then SIGKILL the survivors, then exit with 130.
(4) Exec interface gains a way to register the spawned child with the registry.
(5) Manual smoke test documented in the issue notes; integration test mocks the exec to count termination calls.
(6) Full suite green.
close_reason: Closed

title: Step output is fully buffered, not streamed
description: src/commands/run.ts:189-195 reads child stdout/stderr fully via `new Response(proc.stdout).text()` before writing to the parent. The console reporter doc says step output streams through inherited pipes — it doesn't. Long-running steps (`bun test --watch`, `webpack --progress`, anything with a progress bar) show nothing until they're done. Verbose tools that produce gigabytes (e.g. coverage output) will OOM the parent.
acceptance_criteria:
(1) Child stdio either inherits the parent's pipes (when reporter is plain console + sequential) or is pumped chunk-by-chunk to the parent.
(2) Test verifies streaming by running a step that prints lines on a delay and asserting the parent observed each line before the step exited.
(3) Memory usage stays bounded for steps that produce large output (test asserts the parent doesn't buffer >N MB).
(4) Bug #4 (parallel interleaving) is solved at the same time or filed as a known issue.
(5) Full suite green.
close_reason: Closed

title: Handle git core.quotePath quoted output for non-ASCII paths
description:
Git's default 'core.quotePath=true' setting causes ls-files / diff to emit paths with non-ASCII characters as C-style quoted strings (e.g. "\"caf\303\251.txt\""). createGitRunner currently splits on newlines and passes the verbatim quoted form downstream, where it won't match real filesystem entries.

The fix is to invoke git with '-c core.quotePath=false' so output is always raw UTF-8.

Discovered while auditing implicit invariants in src/runners/files.ts on 2026-04-15.

(1) Every git invocation in createGitRunner threads '-c core.quotePath=false' as the first global arg.
(2) Real-git integration test creates a file with a non-ASCII name (e.g. café.txt), runs git.all() and asserts the path appears unquoted.
(3) Existing fakeSpawner unit tests are updated for the new arg position.
(4) Full suite green.
close_reason: Closed

title: Add repo-root template substitution alias
description:
Add a runtime-provided repo-root template variable so steps can refer to repository-root config files without shelling out to git.

The request proposes `{repo-root}`. The codebase/docs should also reconcile this with the existing documented `{git_root}` token name, which appears to be undocumented in runtime behavior today.
design: If backwards compatibility matters, support one canonical token plus an alias rather than letting docs and runtime drift.
acceptance_criteria:
- step templates can refer to the repository root via a supported token
- docs and runtime agree on the token name(s)
- tests cover substitution from nested workspace execution as well as single-repo execution

title: Document and test requires.file skip behavior
description:
Review the `requires: { file: <path> }` suggestion and lock the intended behavior in docs/tests.

Current repo review suggests this already exists through preflight checks combined with `on-missing: skip` or `warn-skip`. This task should make that path discoverable and prove it with coverage.
design: This is likely documentation/regression coverage rather than a new runtime primitive, but the task should confirm that assumption before closing.
acceptance_criteria:
- docs clearly show how to skip a step when a file is missing using `requires.file` and `on-missing`
- tests cover the missing-file skip path explicitly
- if any runtime gaps are found during review, they are fixed or split into a follow-up bead

title: Add step-level warn-on-failure policy
description:
Add a step-level way to treat a step as informational when its command exits non-zero, without shelling around it with `|| true`.

The user suggestion is an explicit declarative failure policy such as `on-failure: warn`. This work should review how it composes with existing pipeline `continue-on-error`, reporters, and exit-code aggregation.
design: Prefer an explicit policy enum over a bare boolean so future modes remain open (for example: fail, warn, ignore). Keep this separate from preflight `on-missing`, which covers missing prerequisites rather than command failure.
acceptance_criteria:
- config can express an informational step without embedding `|| true` in shell commands
- step summaries/reporting make the warning semantics explicit
- pipeline exit-code behavior is documented and covered by tests

title: Beads pre-commit auto-staging (PLAN §7)
description: Schema has beads.pre-commit: stage|warn|off. Runtime doesn't act on it. When .beads/ is detected and beads.pre-commit is 'stage' (default), the git pre-commit hook dispatcher should git-add any modified .beads/* files before running the pre-commit pipeline so beads changes land in the same commit instead of requiring a follow-up. When 'warn', just print a notice. When 'off', no-op. 100% coverage.
close_reason: Implemented beads pre-commit auto-staging (PLAN §7). New src/integrations/beads/pre-commit.ts with autoStageBeadsChanges(): noop if beads.pre-commit=off or .beads/ missing, 'stage' (default) runs git add on modified .beads/* paths, 'warn' logs without touching the index. Extended GitRunner with modifiedUnder(subPath) (status --porcelain=v1 -z with rename-entry handling) and stage(paths). Wired into dispatchGitHook on pre-commit only (post-* hooks noop). Ran ahead of resolveFiles so the staged file list the pipeline sees includes the beads additions. 16 new tests, 1208 total. Coverage: pre-commit.ts 100%/100%, dispatch.ts 100% lines, files.ts 94.6% funcs / 92% lines.

title: hook <agent> --list: enumerate handlers + currently configured rules (PLAN §4.5)
description: PLAN §4.5 specifies 'agent-hooks hook <agent> --list' to show which handlers exist for the agent and which are currently configured in .config/agent-hooks.yml under agents.<key>.hooks. Extend the hook command: when --list is passed, load config, print handler.hookEvents with a check mark next to the ones that have at least one rule, and also print the matcher + pipeline for each configured rule. Exit 0.
close_reason: Added runHookListCommand() + --list flag to the hook command. Lists every AgentHandler.hookEvents entry with a check mark for configured events, a dot for unconfigured, and '(N rules)' with matcher→pipeline lines per rule. Warns about configured events the handler doesn't recognize (typo detection). Rejects git agent with a helpful pointer to doctor. Rejects unknown agents and config-load failures with exit 2. Commander wires the flag + routes appropriately, with a clear error when hook-name is omitted without --list. 9 new tests. 1191 total passing, hook.ts at 100% funcs / 97.25% lines.

description: git ls-files returns symlinks. A step like `eslint {file}` follows them. Two symlinks pointing at the same target = double-processing or weird failures. Edge case but worth at least documenting.
acceptance_criteria:
(1) Decide on a contract: filter symlinks from the file list, leave them and let steps deal, or add an opt-in flag.
(2) Document in docs/pipelines-and-steps.md.
(3) Test exercises a symlink in a real-git fixture and asserts the documented behavior.
(4) Full suite green.
close_reason: Closed

acceptance_criteria:

(2) On overflow, reject with a clear error.

(4) Add tests that exercise running agent-hooks from a subdir.

title: EPIPE on stdout pipe close (e.g. `agent-hooks ci | head`)
description: Bun doesn't trap EPIPE by default. Piping any agent-hooks command to `head -n 10` will crash with an unhandled EPIPE somewhere in the writer chain when the consumer closes early.
acceptance_criteria:
(1) src/index.ts (or cli.ts) installs a process.on('uncaughtException') handler that swallows EPIPE on stdout/stderr and exits 0.
(2) Test verifies via spawning the CLI and piping to a consumer that closes early — exit code is 0 (or 141, conventionally), not crash.
(3) Full suite green.
close_reason: Not reproducible. Bun handles EPIPE silently and the parent exits 0 or 141. Added a regression test in test/integration/generic.test.ts ('CLI survives a downstream pipe close (EPIPE) without crashing') that pipes the schema output through head -c 1 and asserts no JS error noise on stderr.

title: Spawner should surface signal terminations distinctly from non-zero exits
description:
defaultSpawner returns proc.exited which can be null when the process is killed by a signal (e.g. SIGKILL from OOM). The current 'if (exitCode !== 0)' branch coerces null !== 0 to true and throws a generic 'exited with code null' message, losing the signal context.

Discovered while auditing implicit invariants in src/runners/files.ts on 2026-04-15.
acceptance_criteria:
(1) Spawner result type adds optional 'signal' field.
(2) defaultSpawner reads proc.signalCode (or equivalent Bun API) and populates it.
(3) createGitRunner.run() detects null exitCode + signal and throws a clearer error: 'git ... was killed by SIGXXX'.
(4) Unit test mocks a spawner returning {exitCode: null, signal: 'SIGKILL'} and asserts the wrapped message.
(5) Full suite green.
close_reason: Closed

title: Use NUL-delimited git output for filenames with embedded newlines
description:
createGitRunner.run() splits stdout on newlines, so filenames containing literal newlines (legal on POSIX) split into pieces. Git supports '-z' (NUL-delimited) on ls-files / diff for exactly this case.

Rare but real, and the failure mode is silent corruption rather than a clean error.

Discovered while auditing implicit invariants in src/runners/files.ts on 2026-04-15.
acceptance_criteria:
(1) createGitRunner uses '-z' on ls-files and diff invocations.
(2) Output splitting moves to NUL-byte boundaries.
(3) Real-git integration test creates a file with a literal newline in its name (fs.writeFile) and asserts git.all() returns it as a single entry.
(4) Existing fakeSpawner unit tests are updated for the new arg + NUL-delimited fixture stdout.
(5) Full suite green.
close_reason: Closed
